proto_schema.description: File descriptor set, generated by protoc. To generate, use protoc with imports and source info included. For an example test.proto file, the following command would put the value in a new file named out.pb. $ protoc --include_imports --include_source_info test.proto -o out.pb Structure is [documented below](#nested_proto_schema).
proto_schema.rationale: Structural wrapper for protobuf material; the block itself does not assign IAM—access to tables still requires roles and identities.

proto_descriptors.description: Base64 encoded content of the file.
proto_descriptors.rationale: Encodes schema shape (descriptors) for validation; it is not live application data or an API key. Exposure risk is schema disclosure, not automatic data-plane access without IAM.

schema_bundle_id.description: The unique name of the schema bundle in the form `[_a-zA-Z0-9][-_.a-zA-Z0-9]*`.
schema_bundle_id.rationale: Bundle name only; naming does not embed credentials or replace authentication.

instance.description: The name of the instance to create the schema bundle within.
instance.rationale: Instance reference for where the bundle is registered; not a secret token.

table.description: The name of the table to create the schema bundle within.
table.rationale: Table name linkage only; does not enumerate IAM members or expose row values.

ignore_warnings.description: If true, allow backwards incompatible changes.
ignore_warnings.rationale: Allows breaking schema transitions when explicitly enabled; this is a compatibility/operations toggle, not an IAM or encryption setting—risk is mainly application breakage, not anonymous access.

project.description: If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project ID for API scope; publicly inferable metadata, not a credential.
